{{Short description|Canadian mathematician (1912–2001)}}
'''Cecil James Nesbitt''', Ph.D., F.S.A., M.A.A.A. (1912–2001) was a mathematician who was a Ph.D. student of [[Richard Brauer]] and wrote many influential papers in the early history of [[modular representation theory]]. 

Nesbitt taught [[actuarial science|actuarial mathematics]] at the [[University of Michigan]] from 1938 to 1980.  Nesbitt was born in [[Ontario]], Canada. He received his mathematical education at the [[University of Toronto]] and the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] in [[Princeton, New Jersey|Princeton]].  He served the [[Society of Actuaries]] from 1985 to 1987 as Vice-President for Research and Studies. He developed the [[Schuette–Nesbitt formula]] with [[Donald R. Schuette]].
